transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’m constantly revved up at work, taking on too many projects at once and I can’t slow my mind or my pace down. My employer suggested I get an evaluation because it's starting to affect my job.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually euphoric or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more talkative, impulsive, or overly confident than normal?

Yes, I've been feeling exactly like that for the past several months. I often feel on top of the world but get really snappy, get by on just two hours of sleep while feeling completely wired, and talk way too fast. I've also done some impulsive things lately, like driving way too fast at night and putting thousands of dollars of business books on my credit card.
Have you ever had a separate period of at least 2 weeks when you felt very depressed, lost interest or pleasure in things, or had low energy and hopelessness?

I wouldn't say I felt deeply depressed, but I've had shorter stretches of a couple of weeks where my energy crashed and I felt really flat and unmotivated. During those times, I'd just sit at home staring at my laptop and ignoring my friends, not really caring about doing anything.
During those low periods, did the depressed or flat mood last for at least 2 weeks most of the day nearly every day?

No, it didn't really feel like a constant, deep depression every single day for two weeks straight. It was more like I just ran out of steam and felt flat for a couple of weeks compared to my usual high-energy self.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 full weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day, most of the day?

Yes, during those couple of weeks, that flat feeling and total lack of interest lasted pretty much all day, every day. I couldn't bring myself to do anything, so I just sat staring at my laptop and ignored my friends' invites to hikes or game nights. It wasn't really a crying, sad depression, but more like a complete loss of drive and not caring about anything.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable with less need for sleep, but it did not become severe enough to seriously impair work or require hospitalization?

I definitely have those periods of high energy and barely sleeping, but they actually have caused severe problems at my job. It wasn't mild at all—I've missed deadlines, sent confusing emails, and even got a formal performance review because of it. So it definitely did impair my work.

Have you ever had a period like this that lasted at least 1 week and was severe enough that you needed hospitalization, or caused you to become so impaired that other people were very concerned about your safety or judgment?

Yes, this has been going on for several months now, and though I haven't been hospitalized, it has caused major concern. My parents and boss became really worried about my judgment and behavior, which ultimately led to my formal performance review at work. I've also done some risky things like driving way too fast late at night because I felt invincible and spending way too much money on my credit card.
Have these high-energy, overly confident, and less-sleeping periods lasted at least 1 week at a time, or have they been happening continuously for several months?

They've been happening on and off for most of the past year since I started my full-time job, lasting much longer than just a week. It's been intense and present for more than half of this time, with only a few shorter stretches where I crashed and felt flat.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a sustained manic syndrome with elevated/irritable mood, markedly decreased need for sleep, pressured/rapid speech, racing mind, increased goal-directed activity, and risky impulsive behavior causing clear occupational impairment and concern from others. Symptoms have been present for months, meeting criteria for a manic episode and supporting bipolar affective disorder. A separate depressive episode was also described but is not required for the final diagnosis here.
